Leaning with both arms over the low roof of the boats cabin, the white man said to the steersman, We will spend the night in Arsats clearing, for it is late. <break time="0.8s" /> The steersman only grunted in reply, and the boat moved on up a broad river whose surface shone like metal under the afternoon sun, while the forests on both banks stood motionless. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly the steersman swung the boat at a right angle and drove it through a gap in the bank into a narrow creek, dark and deep like a ditch. <break time="0.8s" /> Immense trees rose on both sides, their roots twisting out of the black water, and the voices of the paddlers echoed strangely in the gloom beneath the leaves. <break time="0.8s" /> At last the creek opened into a wide lagoon, so still and dark that the forest and the evening sky lay reflected on its surface as in a mirror. <break time="0.8s" /> Far across the water stood a small house built on high posts, over whose roof two slender palm trees leaned, and the steersman pointed out Arsats canoe tied beneath it. <break time="0.8s" /> The boatmen would have preferred to sleep anywhere else, for they did not like Arsat, who was a stranger to their country and lived where no one else dared to live. <break time="0.8s" /> It was said that a man who repairs a ruined house and dwells in it shows that he is not afraid to live among the spirits that haunt abandoned places.

The white man had known Arsat years before in a distant country, in times of trouble and danger, and he had come to value the young mans courage and loyalty. <break time="0.8s" /> Since then he had often stopped at this house on his journeys, yet he had never heard how Arsat and the woman had come to live hidden in such a place. <break time="0.8s" /> The sun went down, darkness fell swiftly over the lagoon, and the white man, sitting outside by a fire he had made to keep off the mosquitoes, watched the stars appear. <break time="0.8s" /> Far away across the water, the voices of the boatmen died out one by one, and soon the whole world seemed empty and silent under the cold light of the stars. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking of the dying woman, the white man felt in the darkness a strange mixture of fear and fascination, as if the land around him were a battlefield of phantoms. <break time="0.8s" /> Then Arsat came out and sat down by the fire, and after a long silence he asked, Tuan, do you remember my brother, and the white man answered simply, Yes. <break time="0.8s" /> Tuan, I must tell you everything, Arsat began softly, for a man should share his sorrow with a friend, and what the eye has seen is truth. <break time="0.8s" /> Long ago, he said, he and his brother had served as sword bearers to the Ruler of their country, and in those peaceful days he had fallen secretly in love with Diamelen. <break time="0.8s" /> She was a servant of Inchi Midah, the Rulers wife, so that the lovers could meet only in quick glances and in whispers behind the flowering hedges.
